examples.problem:
| **Number of Hours of Sleep ($x$)** | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Points Scored ($y$)** | $54$ | $68$ | $80$ | $90$ |

A math teacher asked four of her students how many hours they had slept the night before an exam. The information she received is shown in the table above. Compute the covariance of the data sets given that the means are $\overline{x}=5$ and $\overline{y}=73.$
examples.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x=\big\{ x_1,x_2, \ldots, x_n \big\}$ and $y=\big\{ y_1,y_2, \ldots, y_n \big\}$ is given by 

$$
\textrm{Cov}(x,y) =  \dfrac{1}{n} \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})(y_i - \overline{y}),
$$

where $\overline{x} = \dfrac{1}{n} \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^n x_i$ and $\overline{y} = \dfrac{1}{n} \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^n y_i$ are the means of the data sets.

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(2-5)(54-73)+(4-5)(68-73)+(6-5)(80-73)+(8-5)(90-73)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-3)(-19)+(-1)(-5)+(1)(7)+(3)(17)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[57+5+7+51] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 120 \\  & =30.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the following data sets:

$$
x={4,\,-1,\,0,\,5},\,y={6,\,3,\,12,\,11}
$$

You're given that $\overset{―}{x}=2$ and $\overset{―}{y}=8.$ Calculate $\text{Cov}(x,y).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x={{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}}$ and $y={{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(4-2)(6-8)+(-1-2)(3-8)+(0-2)(12-8)+(5-2)(11-8)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(2)(-2)+(-3)(-5)+(-2)(4)+(3)(3)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[-4+15-8+9] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 12 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
